body.p: After the aforesaid amendments, claims 1 and 4-20 are currently pending in the present application, of which claims 16-20 are withdrawn from consideration as being directed to non-elected subject matters.

Independent claim 1 is currently amended to incorporate the limitation "the interface unit is an input element and a detection element, the input element providing at least one of an input basis data and a medical history data of the examinee, and the detection element detecting the examinee to obtain the physiological characteristic and a consciousness state of the examinee," by reference to original claim 3. Accordingly, claim 3 is canceled, and claims 4 to 6 are amended to depend upon the amended independent claim 1.

Further, for clarity, the limitation "the intelligent calculation module is trained by the diagnosis notification based on the examination items" recited in independent claim 1 is amended to read "the intelligent calculation module is retrained by the diagnosis notification based on the examination items," by reference to paragraph [0052] of the specification of the present application. Similarly, the limitation "the intelligent calculation module is trained by the diagnosis notification based on at least one of the response message and the physiological characteristic signal" recited in claim 15 is amended to read "the intelligent calculation module is further retrained by the diagnosis notification based on at least one of the response message and the physiological characteristic signal."

Also, the recitation "... or the interface unit is configured to retrieve one of the physiological characteristic signal and the response message from the examinee" recited in independent claim 1 is deleted, and the term "physiological characteristics" recited in claims 5 and 6 is replaced with "physiological characteristic" to avoid confusion.
Moreover, the term "the physiological characteristic signal" recited in claim 10 is replaced with "the encrypted physiological characteristic signal" for clarity.
In addition to the above amendments, some of the wordings in claims 1, 4, 5, 10, 12, 13, and 14 are revised for better understanding the claimed invention of the present application.
The aforementioned amendments can be fully supported by the original disclosure of the present application. No new matter is being introduced.

Claim 1 is objected to because claim 1 recites "the intelligent calculation module is trained by the diagnosis notification based on the examination items," which should be changed to clarify that the training has been performed prior to diagnosis and/or the system allows for further training.

According to paragraph [0052] of the specification of the present application, it is clear that in order to increase the accuracy of the analysis report, the diagnosis notification of the examiner is returned to the intelligent calculation module for retraining. Therefore, the limitation "the intelligent calculation module is trained by the diagnosis notification based on the examination items" recited in independent claim 1 is amended to read "the intelligent calculation module is retrained by the diagnosis notification based on the examination items" for clarity.
After the aforesaid amendment, the claim objection raised by the examiner should be rendered moot accordingly.

Claims 5 and 15 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112(b) or 35 U.S.C. 112 (pre-AIA), second paragraph, as being indefinite for failing to particularly point out and distinctly claim the subject matter which the inventor or a joint inventor (or for applications subject to pre-AIA 35 U.S.C. 112, the applicant), regards as the invention.

First, it is alleged that claim 5 recites the limitation "physiological characteristics" (plural) in line 2, but claim 5 depends from claims 1 and 3 which recite "physiological characteristic" (singular). It is unclear whether the "characteristics" of claim 5 include the one of claim 1 or not.

In response, the limitation "physiological characteristics" recited in claim 5 has been replaced with "physiological characteristic" for better antecedence. Similarly, the limitation "physiological characteristics" recited in claim 6 has also been replaced with "physiological characteristic."

Further, it is alleged that claim 15 recites the limitation "wherein the intelligent calculation module is trained by the diagnosis notification based on at least one of the response message and the physiological characteristic signal," but claim 15 depends from

claim 1 which recites "the intelligent calculation module is trained by the diagnosis notification based on the examination items." It is unclear and indefinite whether the training of claim 15 replaces the training of claim 1 or is configured to further train the intelligent calculation module based on the response message and the physiological characteristics signal.

According to the claim 15 as originally filed, it is clear that the intelligent calculation module is trained by the diagnosis notification based on at least one of the response message, the physiological characteristic signal and the examination items. Therefore, the limitation "the intelligent calculation module is trained by the diagnosis notification based on at least one of the response message and the physiological characteristic signal" recited in claim 15 is amended to read "the intelligent calculation module is further retrained by the diagnosis notification based on at least one of the response message and the physiological characteristic signal" for clarity.
Hence, Applicant respectfully submits that after the aforementioned amendments to claims 5 and 15, the 35 U.S.C. § 112 rejections should be rendered moot accordingly.

Claims 1, 3-9, and 11-15 are rejected under 35 U.S. C. 103 as being unpatentable over Tang et al. (US Patent Publication No. 2 018/0046773) in view of Jung et al. (US Patent Publication No. 2008/0243005). Claim 10 is rejected under 35 U.S.C. 103 as being unpatentable over Tang and Jung, further in view of Coleman et al. (US Patent Publication No. 2019/0113973).

First, Applicant appreciates the examiner's indication on page 2 of this Office Action that Applicant's arguments in combination with amendments as filed on January 8, 2024 are considered persuasive and the previous 35 U.S.C. 103 rejections have thus been withdrawn.
Regarding the new grounds of the 35 U.S.C. 103 rejections set forth above, Applicant respectfully traverses based at least on the following reasons.

As recited in the amended independent claim 1 of the present application, the claimed invention is directed to a neurological disorders decision support system for assisting an examiner to diagnose an examinee, the neurological disorders decision support system comprising:

a user module comprising an indication unit and an interface unit, the indication unit connected to the interface unit and configured to issue an inquiry to the examinee according to a first indication signal, and the interface unit configured for the examinee to return a response message according to the inquiry and configured to acquire a physiological characteristic related to one or both eves of the examinee to generate a physiological characteristic signal, wherein the interface unit is an input element and a detection element, the input element providing at least one of an input basis data and a medical history data of the examinee, and the detection element detecting the examinee to obtain the physiological characteristic and a consciousness state of the examinee;

a screening module connected to the user module, the screening module configured to generate the first indication signal and output the first indication signal to the indication unit, and the screening module further configured to execute a neurological examination application program and generate a second indication signal according to the response message to the indication unit, wherein the second indication signal is configured to indicate to the examinee to perform a corresponding designated action to obtain the physiological characteristic signal from the interface unit, and the screening module is further configured to output the response message and the physiological characteristic signal, and wherein the neurological examination application program provides a plurality of examination items and selects one or more examination items from the plurality of examination items based on the response message;

an intelligent calculation module connected to the screening module, the intelligent calculation module configured to execute an algorithm to calculate at least one of the response message, the physiological characteristic signal and the examination items to generate an analysis report to the examiner; and

a diagnosis module connected to the intelligent calculation module and the user module, the diagnosis module configured to receive the analysis report for assisting the examiner for diagnosis and send a diagnosis notification to the user module, wherein the diagnosis notification is returned to the intelligent calculation module, and the intelligent calculation module is retrained by the diagnosis notification based on the examination items. (Emphasis added.)

First, Applicant appreciates the examiner's correct observation on page 8 of this Office Action that Tang fails to disclose the acquisition of a physiological characteristic related to one or both eves of the examinee to generate a physiological characteristic signal, nor the limitation that the neurological examination application program provides a plurality of examination items and selects one or more examination items from the plurality of examination items based on the response message.

In addition to the distinguishing limitations indicated above, Applicant respectfully submits that nowhere in Tang discloses the detection of the examinee to obtain the physiological characteristic and a consciousness state of the examinee and the indication to the examinee to perform a corresponding designated action to obtain the physiological characteristic signal, as recited in the amended independent claim 1 of this application. Moreover, since Tang fails to disclose that the claimed neurological examination application program of the present application provides a plurality of examination items as recognized above, Tang also cannot disclose that the claimed intelligent calculation module of the present application is retrained by the diagnosis notification based on the examination items, as recited in the amended independent claim
1 of the present application.

Particularly, paragraph [0033] of Tang simply discloses an interaction interface 140 that includes an input device (e.g., a touch panel, a keyboard, a microphone, a scanner or a flash memory reader) for user to type text commands, give voice commands or upload some related data (e.g., images, medical records, or personal examination reports) and is totally silent on detecting the examinee to obtain the physiological characteristic and a consciousness state of the examinee as claimed in the present application. Furthermore, referring to paragraph [0040] of Tang, it should be noted that the interaction interface 140 disclosed in Tang is configured for receiving responses Sans corresponding to the symptom inquiries Sqry, and then the prediction module 124 disclosed in Tang is configured to generate a result prediction, such as at least one disease prediction PDT (e.g., a disease name or a list of disease names ranked by their probabilities) or/and at least one medical department suggestion matching the possible disease according to the prediction model MDL, the initial symptom Sini and the responses Sans. Hence, Tang also fails to indicate to the examinee to perform a corresponding designated action to obtain the physiological characteristic signal as claimed in the present application.

As to Jung, it is directed to a computational user-health testing. Referring to paragraphs [0085] to [0088] of Jung's disclosure, it is clear that Jung simply provides a user-health test function selection module 138 for selecting, e.g., a cranial nerve test function, based on user-health data, wherein the cranial nerve test function includes one or more visual field test functions, one or more eye movement test functions, one or more pupil movement test functions, one or more face pattern test functions, one or more hearing test functions, and/or one or more voice test functions.
Obviously, Jung fails to disclose a user module that includes an interface unit to acquire a physiological characteristic related to one or both eves of the examinee to

generate at least one of a physiological characteristic signal, not to mention to teach or suggest that the interface unit is a detection element for detecting the examinee to obtain the physiological characteristic and a consciousness state of the examinee.

Moreover, nowhere in Jung discloses a screening module for generating a second indication signal that is configured to indicate to the examinee to perform a corresponding designated action to obtain the physiological characteristic signal from the interface unit, nor an intelligent calculation module that can be retrained by the diagnosis notification based on the examination items as achieved by the claimed invention of the present application. Therefore, Jung cannot cure the aforementioned deficiencies of Tang, and thus the proposed combination of Tang and Jung still cannot render obvious the claimed invention recited in the amended independent claim 1 of the present application.

Regarding Coleman, it is only cited to be in combination with Tang and Jung for the §103 rejection of dependent claim 10. Specifically, Coleman is directed to a computer network implemented system for improving the operation of one or more biofeedback computer systems. However, similar to Tang and Jung, Coleman completely fails to provide any teachings or suggestions that relate the eye of an examinee to a neurological disorder as claimed in the present application. Moreover, Coleman also does not disclose the diagnosis module of the claimed invention that is configured to receive an analysis report for assisting the examiner for diagnosis and send a diagnosis notification to the user module, wherein the diagnosis notification is returned to the intelligent calculation module, and the intelligent calculation module is retrained by the diagnosis notification based on the examination items. Therefore, Coleman still cannot remedy the aforementioned deficiencies of Tang and Jung to render obvious the claimed invention of the present application.

Given the foregoing, Applicant respectfully submits that Tang, alone or in combination with Jung and Coleman, cannot render obvious the claimed invention recited in the amended independent claim 1 of the present application. Hence, the amended independent claim 1 and the dependent claims thereof are patentably distinct over the cited references. Accordingly, reconsideration and withdrawal of the § 103 rejections are respectfully requested.

For further reference, the corresponding counterparts of the present application have been granted and issued in Japan as JP7362138B2 on October 17, 2023 and in Taiwan as TWI823015B on November 21, 2023.

Applicant expresses his gratitude to Examiner for the courtesies extended to the Applicant's undersigned representative throughout prosecution of this application. In view of the foregoing, Applicant respectfully submits that each of the pending rejections has been overcome, leaving the present application in condition for allowance. A consideration to that effect is respectfully requested.
Respectfully submitted,
